subject: general
question:
The diagram below shows a part of the human alimentary canal. Which process is taking place and how?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a83a192034fe85791999bac393478c3cabcc7cb95e6663263021cf95c68c1d31.png]

options.text: Peristalsis, due to rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscular walls
Digestion, due to rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscular walls

solution:
The correct answer is __**Peristalsis, due to rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscular walls**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The alimentary canal is a long, tube-like structure that runs from the mouth to the anus.
 
• The alimentary canal plays an important role in human digestion, hence it is also termed as the digestive tract.
 
• The primary organs of the alimentary canal are - the mouth and buccal cavity, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine.
 
• The alimentary canal is also associated with digestive glands such as salivary glands, pancreas, and liver.
 
• The adrenal gland is an endocrine gland but is not associated with the alimentary canal.
 
• The adrenal glands are located on top of both kidneys, thus these are commonly called suprarenal glands.
 
• The gland has two parts - the adrenal medulla and the adrenal cortex.
 
• Both the medulla and cortex secrete different types pf hormones.
 
• The adrenal medulla secretes two types of hormones - Adrenaline (epinephrine) and Noradrenaline (norepinephrine).
 
• Adrenaline and Noradrenaline are known as emergency or 'Fight or Flight' hormones.
 
• The adrenal cortex produces a variety of hormones viz., glucocorticoids such as corticosterone, cortisol, etc., mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone, and adrenal androgens.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pancreas-

 
 
• It acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland.
 
• The exocrine pancreas secretes digestive enzymes and the endocrine part secretes hormones.
 
• The digestive enzymes such as amylase, proteases, and lipase are secreted by the pancreas into the duodenum.
 
• Islets of Langerhans are present in the pancreas that secrete hormones such as Insulin, Glucagon, and Somatostatin into the blood.
 
 
 
• Liver-
 
 
• The liver is located in the upper right region of the abdomen.
 
• It is the largest digestive gland.
 
• The liver secretes bile juice that is stored by the gall bladder.
 
• Bile helps in the emulsification of fats and the digestion of vitamins and cholesterol.
 
 
 
• Salivary gland-
 
 
• The salivary gland secretes digestive juice saliva in the buccal cavity.
 
• Saliva has three digestive enzymes- lingual lipase, salivary amylase, and maltase.
